problem: Zero-shot ObjectNav methods (e.g. the LLM-frontier baseline L3MVN) are holistic and ignore recurring failure modes: collisions/getting trapped, stale long-term goals that waste exploration, and misidentified targets from semantic segmentation.
motivation: Failure analysis of the L3MVN baseline shows that collision, low exploration efficiency and false target detection account for a large share of failed episodes. Targeted, dynamically triggered helpers for each failure case can raise success without any training.
key_idea: Add three dynamically triggered helper modules (cluster-based Collision Helper, LLM-sleep Exploration Helper, VLM-based Detection Helper) to an LLM-frontier zero-shot ObjectNav global policy.
insight: Each helper reduces its own failure category in the HM3D ablation (collision failures 19.10% to 13.10% with the Collision Helper alone; false detection 16.95% to 13.90% with the Detection Helper alone), and SR rises from 0.505 to 0.565 with all three. However, the full system increases exploration failures (13.65% to 21.25%) because masking false targets and long-range exploration hinder multi-floor search. Manual double-checking shows that many detection 'failures' are simulator misjudgments.
method: Semantic map + frontier map: RGB-D and pose are turned into a top-down semantic map (obstacle, explored, agent position, object channels, plus a false-target channel); frontiers are extracted and scored by cost/utility
LLM frontier selection: following L3MVN, an LLM is prompted with the objects near each frontier and the target to score P(F_i), and the argmax frontier F_LLM is chosen

Collision Helper: when the agent moves under 25 cm on a forward action or the local planner finds no path, it computes the largest connected component of the navigable (explored) area and uses its centroid as the long-term goal to untrap
Exploration Helper: if the distance d between the agent and the long-term goal is under 50 cm and F_LLM has not changed, the LLM is put to sleep for 20 steps so the agent explores freely

Detection Helper: when segmentation detects the target, quantized Qwen-VL-Chat-Int4 verifies it with a yes/no prompt; a true target becomes the final goal, a false one is masked and recorded, and after 400 steps a recorded false target is used as the final goal
Local policy: Fast Marching Method path planning to the long-term goal (updated every 10 steps), with no training; segmentation uses RedNet and YOLOv8

setting.backbone: RoBERTa-based LLM for frontier scoring (as in L3MVN), Qwen-VL-Chat-Int4 as the VLM (all frozen), RedNet + YOLOv8 for segmentation, FMM planner
setting.action_space: low-level: move forward 25 cm, turn left/right 30°, look up/down, stop

numbers.extra: manually double-checked detection failures caused by simulator misjudgment; not a standard evaluation

numbers.eval_set_note: SemExp Gibson ObjectNav validation split, 5 scenes

numbers_note: Ablation table (Table II) gives HM3D SR for single-helper variants: Collision 0.530, Exploration 0.531, Detection 0.540, no helper 0.505. The paper says 'validation' split for both datasets; the mapped split name is 'val'.
results: TriHelper reaches SR 0.565 / SPL 0.253 on HM3D and SR 0.852 / SPL 0.431 on Gibson, beating the L3MVN baseline (0.504 / 0.231 on HM3D; 0.761 / 0.377 on Gibson). It also surpasses VLFM in SR on HM3D (0.525) and Gibson (0.840), although its SPL is lower than VLFM's (0.304 on HM3D, 0.522 on Gibson). With manual correction of simulator misjudgments SR is 0.620 on HM3D.
limitations: Exploration failures increase (13.65% to 21.25%) because the agent struggles to change floors and false-target masking delays finding the target
SPL is lower than VLFM's, since rejecting false targets lengthens paths
The manual double-check results are not a standard protocol and were applied only to HM3D; only simulation evaluation, with an extra VLM adding compute
